subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Base Rate Neglect
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Base Rate Neglect.

hook.text: A cab hit someone at night. A witness said it was blue. The city has 85% green cabs. Was it really blue?

buildup.text: Most people say blue because the witness seems reliable. They forget that green cabs outnumber blue ones 5 to 1.

discovery.text: Base rate neglect: we overweight vivid evidence and underweight boring background statistics.

twist.text: Even trained doctors fall for it. A positive test with 5% false positive rate in a rare disease is usually wrong.

climax.text: Before trusting vivid evidence, check the base rate first. Frequency matters more than your gut feeling.

punchline.text: The boring statistic usually beats the dramatic story.

quiz.question: What is base rate neglect?
options: Overweighting vivid evidence while ignoring background frequency
Always trusting the base rate over witnesses

details.summary: Base rate neglect as a decision trap causes people to make probability judgments based on vivid specific information while ignoring the underlying statistical frequency. This leads to systematic overreaction to dramatic cases and under-reaction to common patterns.
details.whyItMatters: Investment decisions, hiring choices, and risk assessments are all distorted when base rates are ignored. A vivid success story makes a business opportunity seem likely even when the base rate of success in that industry is very low.
takeaways: Specific vivid information dominates over statistical background rates
People overestimate the chance of rare events when given detailed case information
Asking how common this type of outcome is overall helps correct the trap

faq.question: How does base rate neglect affect investment decisions?
faq.answer: Investors hear a compelling startup story and invest based on the narrative's plausibility, ignoring that 90 percent of startups fail. The vivid business plan and passionate founder override the statistical reality of extremely low success rates.

faq.question: What is the simplest way to avoid base rate neglect?
faq.answer: Before evaluating any specific case, look up the base rate. What percentage of similar ventures succeed? What percentage of similar symptoms indicate the disease? Starting with the base rate and adjusting for specifics produces far better estimates.
